textile.title: Single-sided, rectangular body stamp made from wood. Stamp design is a geometric M-shape.
Double-sided, roughly rectangular body stamp made of wood. One side has a design with two animal figures and lines, and the other with two frogs or toads.
Cotton hammock made of twisted cord. Each end comes together in a bundle with cord wrapped around it; 17 tassels on one side where the cord has been sewn across perpendicularly.
Wooden spindle. Whorl is a flat disc of wood or possible seed. The spindle shaft is thickened in the centre.
Sincu. Cheese mould made by Panare for local peasants. Flat woven mat with chevron design, rolled and tied with synthetic string.
Single-sided, rectangular body stamp made of wood; design of vertical lines.
Single-sided, rectangular body stamp made of wood. Design of carved lines forming a geometric pattern.
Single-sided, rectangular body stamp made of wood. Design of circles and geometric lines, some forming an X-shape in the centre of the stamp.
Single-sided, rectangular body stamp made of wood. Design of carved chevrons, circles and geometric shapes.

household.title: Wapa, or basketry tray. Round, shallow tray, with woven geometric design in black and light brown. The outer edge of the tray is supported with a cane ring frame on the top and bottom, tied on with fibre.
Manioc sieve. Circular with frame made of bundled fibres, woven with a central diamond design.

Tawahemen. Woven black and white basket with circular rim and square base. Cane around rim, attached with fibre string. Ankatapuhpe (traditional Panare) design with modern Panare weave pattern (one over three).

Tawahemen. Woven black and white basket with circular rim and square base. Cane around rim, attached with fibre string; string forms a small loop on one side, possibly used as a handle. Yekwanoid (modern Panare) design.
Tawahemen. Woven black and white basket with circular rim and square base. Cane around rim, attached with fibre string. Yekwanoid (modern Panare) design.
Tawahemen. Woven red and white basket with circular rim and square base. Cane around rim, attached with fibre string. Traditional Panare design.
Tawahemen. Woven black and white basket with circular rim and square base. Cane around rim, attached with fibre string. Traditional Panare design.
Pegall. Small woven black and white basket (A) with lid (B). Top of lid and base of basket are square-shaped. Modern Panare design.

Ewey. Open-weave basket with circular rim and hexagonal base. Basket attached to cane rim with twisted string, which extends into a string handle. Previously used; two small breaks in basketry near base; string unravelling in places; some black residue on interior.
Ewey. Open-weave cylindrical basket with narrow circular rim and hexagonal base. Weaving unravelling slightly on interior of rim.

Ewey. Deep basket made of open work cane with a wide mouth, slight shoulder and square base. Ring of cane around the rim, attached to the basket with string, with a small string handle attached to both sides of the basket. Some of the cane has been painted to create a geometric pattern.

Tawa or plaited carrying basket made from cucurito palm. Excess fibres tied in a knot at the base; darker plant fibre used to reinforce the rim and form a handle which is tied onto the rim at two points.
Pape. Fire fan made from interwoven cucurito palm, square in shape, with a handle made from loose palm strands bound together with fibre.
Half of a gourd, with a broadly oval shaped body and a black coated inner surface. Used for eating and drinking.
Broom made from stalks on which fruits of coroba palm grow.
Wooden cooking spatula with flat paddle; straight sides and rounded end. The handle is flat and narrow with a flaring terminal.
Wooden shedstick, beater or weaving sword. Elongated oval with pointed oval cross-section. Decorated with sporadic incised lines which may have resulted from use.
Kerosene lamp, made from a repurposed old tin can. The can is white and has 'Liga para Frenos' written on it. The fibre wick protrudes from the top through a hole in the can's red metal screw cap.
Un-woven basketry elements. Black on one face, pale on the other.

Wooden, painted toy bow with cotton two ply twist string. Painted with red and black dots and lines; notch carved in one end. Two splits in the wood, one almost the entire length of the back. Made for tourists; part of a set with arrows 1982.865 B-C.

Kamawa', or shoulder bag, made of tree anteater hide, used by men for ammunition etc. The main body of the bag is rectangular and has coarse, dark brown fur. The bag is held closed by a catch, formed from the animal's lighter brown tail, which is wrapped round the bag; a wooden peg which fits through a hole in the tail forms the fastening. A string shoulder strap is affixed to the top corners.

Kamawa', or shoulder bag. The bag is rectangular and made from spotted animal hide, possibly jaguar. A triangular flap at the front of the bag has a knotted string threaded through it. A string shoulder strap is affixed to the top corners using red thread, which has also been used to stitch up the side seams.
Ya'ara pujpe. Stool made from a tortoise shell.
Ewe. Open-weave waisted basket with circular rim and hexagonal base. Slight wear visible on exterior of basket in places.

Pinya. Fishing harpoon or spear with barbed point. Long wooden shaft with circular cross-section tapering towards the butt; shaft also tapers slightly towards the top which is socketed; narrow point with a single barb, fixed in place with cord and resin; band of black resin around the shaft near the point and on the butt.

ceramic.title: Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with crosses. Small loop of fibre attached to the cane.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with crosses. Small loop of fibre attached to the cane. Weave has split in one area below the rim.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Natural and painted yellow fibres plaited into geometric pattern; the outside of the basket is undecorated. Loop of dark brown fibre attached to the frame.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited brown and natural geometric pattern and a central square with four frog motifs. Loop of thin fibre attached to the frame.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with a central square with four monkey motifs and a pattern of triangles and lines above and below. Small loop of fibre attached to the frame.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural pattern of anthropomorphic motifs within rectangles. Small loop of fibre attached to the frame.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural with six rows of centipede motifs within squares. Thin loop of fibre attached to the frame.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with two central rows of dog motifs within squares. Small loop of fibre attached to the frame.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with four central rows of monkey motifs within squares, and a row of lizards at the top and bottom.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with two central rows of lizard motifs within squares.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with black frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with four cat motifs within squares.
Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited dark brown and natural geometric pattern.

Wapa. A shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with triangles connected by lines. Small loop of fibre attached to the frame.

Wapa. A small, shallow, round tray made from plaited basketry with frames of cane attached by fibre to the inside and outside of the rim. Plaited black and natural geometric pattern with four central lizard motifs within squares. Small loop of fibre attached to the cane.

Mankowaye. Curare pot. Wrapped in leaves and tied with thread. Presumed to contain curare, a broad term for various alkaloid arrow poisons produced from plant extracts. Used as a paralysing agent in hunting

sculpture.title: Manioc press. An imitation or model made for tourists, some canes painted black and red. Attachment loop at one end, two openings through the opposite end.

garment.title: Areko. Circular headdress. Made of a layered plaited headband, possibly leaf, with a double frame of wood or cane. The feathers are held together with fibre and fit between the two layers. A leaf bundle is present, to be suspended down the back. There are five feathers detached but present.
Dance belt made of tree bark and decorated with a black pigment in a diamond pattern.

arms.title: Quiver and darts for use with a blow gun. Quiver made from a hollowed length of bamboo, one end stuffed with cotton or cotton palm fibre; basketry collar made from black and plain cane strips attached near the middle of the quiver and flaring towards the top. Darts present in one end, three wrapped with cotton and fibre.

Quiver and darts for use with a blow gun. Quiver made from a hollowed length of bamboo, one end stuffed with cotton or cotton palm fibre. Darts arranged around the circumference of the quiver and slightly protruding; centre stuffed with leaves and cotton.

Renciste. Hunting lance or spear with metal blade. Long wooden shaft with circular cross-section, tapering slightly towards the butt; long, angular blade set into a slot in the shaft and bound in place with plant fibre cord wrapping.

Watta. Blowpipe or blow gun made from two long lengths of cane, the narrowest one sliding inside the largest one. Flared mouthpiece secured to the pipe with resin or gum. At the end of the blowpipe is a stopper of resign or gum preventing the wider cane tube from sliding out.

jewelry.title: Ear adornments made from metal triangles made from repurposed Pepsi Cola cans threaded onto fine strings with glass beads. Beads alternate between light blue and white, with one strand having a single red bead; both earrings have one dark blue bead. Earrings are kept together with knotted string.

other.title: Back pack made from woven cucurito palm with bamboo or cane frame; carrying strap made from strips of bark. Open-fronted with bark strips threaded across the opening.

Oyaru or back pack with wooden frame and woven back, possibly of leather. Furred hide straps attached in four places, knotted together in two places. There are also bark straps attached in four places. The leather, bark and hide straps are stiff and frayed in places. There are two dark stains; one in the centre of the pack, and one at the top, which extends to the bark strap.

Panayerekon. Two ear adornments, made of red, green, yellow and black parrot and toucan feathers. Bundles of feathers are attached to thin sticks with string. Sticks are held together with two sticking plasters.
Panayo. Ear piercing instrument. Coloured red for piercing the ears of females. Formed of sharpened, crossed skewers with diamond of woven wool in the centre.
